stem:
A 25-year-old student notices hunger pangs and increased gastric secretion while smelling bread baking, before she has eaten anything.

Which of the following phases of gastric secretion does this illustrate?

options.label: A
options.misconception: A food-in-stomach phase is being applied before any food has been eaten.
options.explanation: The gastric phase is set in motion by the entry of food into the stomach, which triggers local neural and hormonal mechanisms; here no food has been swallowed.

options.label: B
options.misconception: A downstream phase is being applied to a pre-ingestion stimulus.
options.explanation: The intestinal phase begins when chyme reaches the duodenum and modulates further gastric activity; it cannot be triggered by the smell of food.

options.label: C
options.misconception: An inter-digestive motility pattern is being cast as a secretory phase.
options.explanation: The migrating motility complex is a pattern of peristalsis that sweeps the empty gut between meals, initiated by motilin; it is not a secretory response to food cues.

options.label: D
options.misconception: A hindgut event is being cast as a gastric secretory phase.
options.explanation: Colonic filling occurs hours after a meal as residue reaches the large intestine; it has no role in the secretory response to the smell of food.

options.label: E
options.misconception: None; the sight and smell of food trigger the cephalic phase.
options.explanation: The cephalic (reflex) phase of gastric secretion takes place before food enters the stomach and is triggered by the smell, taste, sight, or thought of food.

context: Learning objective: the three phases of gastric secretion. Cephalic: sight/smell/taste/thought of food before eating (vagal reflex). Gastric: food enters the stomach (distention, local reflexes, gastrin; lasts 3-4 hours). Intestinal: chyme enters the duodenum (secretin, CCK, entero-gastric inhibition).
